intro.heading: The audit is finished. Has anyone but the auditor seen it?
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: A senior carer has spent the afternoon on the monthly medicines audit. She has answered every question, taken photos of the fridge and the storage room, and signed her name. The report is saved and the audit counts as done. The registered manager is on the floor and has not seen a single answer. Three of the No answers were marked as fine, and nobody else has looked at them. A quality audit is only as good as the person who last read it, and an inspector will ask who that was.

trail.text: A senior carer works through the monthly medicines audit.
She answers every question and photographs the storage room.
She signs, the score is calculated and the report is saved.
The manager is on a late shift. Nobody has opened the answers.
Each was marked as acceptable. Nobody else has agreed.
A different auditor repeats the audit and marks the same items differently.
A good score, and no record that she ever read it.
“Who reviewed this audit, and what did they decide?”

trail_close: The audit was done properly. The gap is a review. Here is how an optional sign off in CareStream gives each audit a second pair of eyes, and where it stops.

why.heading: An audit marked by one person is one person's view
why.sub: A second look is not a rule. It is a habit many managers choose to keep.

cards.title: One auditor, one judgement
cards.body: A No answer can be a real gap or a reasonable choice. The auditor has to decide, and another person may decide differently.

cards.title: A score is not a review
cards.body: A high score looks reassuring. It does not show that the person accountable for the service read the answers behind it.

cards.title: Reviews slip when they live in email
cards.body: Asking for a report to be forwarded works until the week it is forgotten. Then nobody can say which audits were checked.

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: Do we have to have a manager sign off on audits?
items.a: No. It is optional, and it is off until you switch it on in Settings. Some services like a second pair of eyes on every audit. Others trust their auditors and review the trends instead. CareStream lets you choose.

items.q: How does audit approval work day to day?
items.a: Someone completes an audit and signs it. It goes to your care manager or registered manager, who gets an email and opens the Audit sign-off view in the Staff Hub. They read the answers, then approve with a drawn signature or send it back with a note.

CareStream matches on job title. Anyone whose title includes care manager or registered manager can sign off. It is not a separate permission level, so make sure the right people have the right title on their staff record.

items.q: What happens if I send an audit back?
items.a: You must add a note saying what to change. The audit reopens, the auditor amends it and completes it again, and it comes back to you for sign off.

items.q: When do we get the audit report?
items.a: With sign off on, the PDF report is created when the manager approves it and is emailed to admins. With sign off off, it is created as soon as the audit is completed. It includes scores, answers, photos, actions and signatures.

items.q: Does the sign off cost extra, or need a bigger plan?
items.a: No. The audit library, scoring, photos, reports, actions, scheduling and the sign off all work on every plan, including the free one. The recommendations from our own technology are the part that needs a paid plan. You can try a paid plan free for 14 days, or create a free account and start with audits.

items.q: Does a signed off audit mean we are compliant with CQC?
items.a: No. Scores are CareStream's own and are not a CQC rating, and an audit is not something you submit to the regulator. The sign off shows that your service looks at its own work. It sits with the rest of your CQC evidence.

items.q: Can a weak audit result lead to training?
items.a: Yes, in a hands on way. If a question keeps failing, you can allocate short training on that topic from your own policies. That step is yours to take, because an audit result does not allocate anything by itself.

faqs.heading: Audit sign off in CareStream, answered

items.q: What is an audit sign off?
items.a: It is a manager's check on a completed audit. They read the answers, then approve it with their name, role, date and drawn signature, or send it back to the auditor with a note.

items.q: Is audit approval on by default?
items.a: No. Audit approval is off until you switch it on in Settings. Until then, audits finish as normal and the report is created straight away.

items.q: Who can give a manager sign off?
items.a: Anyone whose job title matches care manager or registered manager. They see an Audit sign-off view in the Staff Hub, and get an email each time one is ready.

items.q: Does the audit report change when sign off is on?
items.a: Only the timing. With sign off on, the audit report is created when the manager approves it, and then emailed to admins. It includes the scores, every answer, photos, actions and signatures.

items.q: Is the sign off available on the free plan?
items.a: Yes. Audits are free on every plan, including the sign off. Recommendations from our own technology need a paid plan. See pricing for the plans.

items.q: What does a good quality audit look like?
items.a: It asks the same questions each time, scores them the same way, records evidence such as photos, turns every failure into an action with an owner and a date, and is reviewed by someone other than the auditor. Browse the audit library for examples.

items.q: Does the law say audits need a manager sign off?
items.a: No. Regulation 17 on good governance requires systems and processes that are established and operated effectively, but it does not say who must sign each audit. How you review audits is your decision.

items.q: Why would an inspector care about a quality audit?
items.a: Providers must assess, monitor and improve the quality and safety of their services. Audits are one way to show you do that, and a record of who reviewed them and what they decided shows the loop was closed.

items.q: Can I show the audit approval history?
items.a: Yes. The Audit sign-off view lists recently approved audits with who approved them and when, and the saved audit carries the manager's name, role, date and signature.

guide.heading: A practical way to add a second review to your audits
guide.lede: A manager sign off only helps if it is quick, consistent and kept. Here is a way to set one up that does not slow your audits down.

sections.h3: Decide what the manager is checking
paragraphs: A review is not a re-do. The manager is not repeating the audit. They are checking that the answers make sense, the evidence is there and each failure has an action. Agree that list with your auditors first, so a send back is no surprise.
Be clear about the difference between a No that is acceptable and a No that is a gap. The auditor has to classify it, and the reviewer is the person who can challenge it.

sections.h3: Four habits that keep the sign off useful
checklist: Check job titles first: the person who signs off must have care manager or registered manager in their title.
Review within a few days, while the auditor remembers the room, and leave a note whenever you send one back.
Look at the pattern, not just the page: open the trends and repeat failures once a month.
Turn repeat failures into action: a gap that keeps coming back may need short training or a policy change.

guide.note: For the inspector. Keep the audit, the manager's name and date, and the actions that followed together, so you can show that someone other than the auditor reviewed the result. Remember that the scores are CareStream's own and not a CQC rating.
